Executive Order 12396 of December 9, 1982, section 5(a), revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621 but not (o), so section 1 of EO 11294 survived that amendment (later event, no end). Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 revoked subsection (o) in its section 1 and, in section 3, revoked Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966; the express revocation of the order on July 1, 1986 is the first end of this clause.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11294
DELEGATING CERTAIN AUTHORITY OF THE PRESIDENT TO ESTABLISH
MAXIMUM PER DIEM RATES FOR GOVERNMENT CIVILIAN PERSON­
NEL IN TRAVEL STATUS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Executive Order No. 10621 of July 1, 1955, entitled 
“Delegation of Certain Functions of the President to the Secretary of 
Defense,” is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph at the 
end of Section 1 thereof:
“ (o) The authority vested in the President by section 3 of the Travel 
Expense Act of 1949,63 Stat. 166, as amended (5 U.S.C. 836), to estab­
lish maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and 
employees of the Government to the extent that such authority per­
tains to travel status in localities in Alaska, Hawaii, the Common­
wealth of Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, and possessions of the United 
States.”
S ec. 2. -There is hereby delegated to the Secretary of State the 
authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the Travel Expense 
Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 166, as amended (5 U.S.C. 836), to establish 
maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and em­
ployees of the Government to the extent that such authority pertains 
to travel status in localities in any area (including the Trust Territory 
of the Pacific Islands) situated outside the United States, the Common­
wealth of Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, and the possessions of the 
United States.
S ec. 3. Executive Order No. 11230 of June 28,1965, entitled “Dele­
gating Certain Functions of the President to the Director of the 
Bureau of the Budget,” as amended, is hereby further amended by 
substituting for paragraph (9) of Section 1 thereof the following:
“ (9) The authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the 
Travel Expense Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 166 (5 U.S.C. 836}, to establish 
maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and em­
ployees of the Government to the extent that such authority pertains 
to travel status of such officers and employees while en route to, from, 
or between localities situated outside the 48 contiguous states of the 
United States and the District of Columbia.”
S ec. 4. T o the extent not heretofore superseded, Executive Order 
No. 10970 of October 27,1961, is hereby superseded.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T he  W h ite H ouse,
August 4 >  1966.
[F.R. Doc. 66-8687; Filed, Aug. 5, 1966, 2:03 p.m.]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 153— TUESDAY, AUGUST 9, 1966

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11294 of August 4, 1966 (31 FR 10601) has four sections, all read in the held Federal Register text: section 1 amends Executive Order 10621 by adding paragraph (o) (the President's authority under section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 to set maximum per diem rates in Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions, delegated to the Secretary of Defense); section 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the same authority for areas outside the United States; section 3 amends paragraph (9) of Section 1 of Executive Order 11230 (the same authority for travel to and between places outside the 48 contiguous States, delegated to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget); and section 4 supersedes Executive Order 10970, to the extent not heretofore superseded. Two later orders act on it. Executive Order 11609 of July 22, 1971, section 11, lists among the orders hereby superseded Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966 (together with Executive Order 11230 that it amended); section 12 makes the order effective immediately except paragraphs (1) to (13) and (19) of its section 1, so the supersession of section 3 took effect on July 22, 1971 (the machine lead of October 20, 1971 is the ninety-day date for those paragraphs of section 1, which does not include section 11). Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 (51 FR 24299), section 1 revokes subsection (o) of Section 1 of EO 10621 (the paragraph section 1 of EO 11294 added), section 2 re-delegates the per diem authority to the Secretary of State under section 102(a) of the Federal Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses Act of 1985, and section 3 states that Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966, is revoked. That express revocation of the whole order on July 1, 1986 ends sections 1, 2 and 4, and is the latest clause end, so the whole order ended on July 1, 1986. Executive Order 12396 of December 9, 1982 revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621 but not subsection (o), so it did not end section 1. The held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) agrees: it says EO 11294, as amended by EO 11609, was revoked by EO 12561. The Federal Register disposition note held for EO 11294 gives EO 10960 of October 27, 1961 as the order superseded, but the order's text (and EO 10970 of October 27, 1961) says 10970; the text controls. The machine lead naming EO 11488 is an unrelated land order that does not cite EO 11294 and is disregarded. Status recommended: no.

savings_residuals.reason: The delegated per diem authority did not lapse: Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 re-delegated it in sections 1 and 2 under the 1985 Act, so the function continues under that order's own authority, and the supersession of EO 10970 in section 4 and the earlier amendments of EO 10621 and EO 11230 are accrued effects that no longer depend on EO 11294.
